topic: Claude explained like you're 5: six basics lessons with prompts, drawn from the /learn guides
audience: Professionals starting with Claude or stuck at the basics
goal: Re-learn the basics and open one guide on mojeedabisiga.com/learn
notes: From the guide Skill, project, instructions or connector?: custom instructions hold general preferences and apply to every conversation (put: how plain the language, how long answers, words you never want; don't put: steps of one particular job). Example: 'Write in plain English. Keep answers short. Ask me before you assume anything about my work.'

Projects hold background documents and knowledge, and apply only to chats inside that project (files for one client, one course, one big piece of work). Don't put a job you repeat everywhere in a project. Example: 'Using the files here, summarise what changed this month.'

Connectors (MCP) give Claude access to other apps and data such as your drive or calendar, and apply when Claude needs that app. A connector gives access; it doesn't teach Claude how you want a job done.

Skills: a way of doing one particular job, applying only when a request needs it, in any chat. A small folder of instructions (sometimes scripts and templates) with a name and a description; Claude reads the description to decide when to use it. Skills load in layers, so many don't slow Claude down. Rule: once you've explained the same thing three times, make it a skill.

From the guide Brief Claude like a new colleague: a one-line prompt leaves Claude to fill in everything you didn't say, so it picks the safe, middle-of-the-road answer written for nobody in particular. Every detail you add replaces a guess with a fact.

The five parts: the goal (what it's for, not just the task), the background (who it's for, what they know, what happened), the material (paste or attach the notes, numbers, draft), the shape (length, format, tone, order), the finish line (what done means, and what to do if something's missing: list it instead of guessing).

Example: one line 'Write me a report on our Ghana sales.' vs a brief: help the board decide whether to keep selling in Ghana; they meet Friday, have seen last quarter's numbers, two members want to pull out; work only from the attached sheet; one page, three options (stay, shrink, pull out) each with cost and main risk, recommendation at the top, plain English; done when every number comes from the sheet; list anything missing at the end instead of guessing.
Ask me first prompt: 'Before you start, ask me the five questions you most need answered to do this well. Wait for my answers.'
Show what good looks like: paste a past example ('Match this format'); one example beats a paragraph of adjectives.

Describe-first prompt: 'Before answering anything, describe this file: 1. How many rows and columns, and what each column contains. 2. The date range. 3. Missing values, numbers stored as text, and repeated rows. 4. Anything that looks like a totals row or a second table. Don't analyse anything yet.'
Define your terms: which column (Net_Amount, not Gross), which rows (leave out Status = Cancelled), which dates (July to September 2026), which unit.

Show the working: 'Show your working: list each step, the number of rows after each step, and the formula you used. Then give the answer.' Row counts expose problems: 4,812 rows becoming 9,624 after a join means something went wrong.

Check it two ways: ask for the same number another way (pivot table vs formula); spot-check three rows by hand; sanity-check against what you know. Ask: 'What could make this answer wrong? List the three most likely problems.'
Five traps: numbers stored as text, repeated rows, totals counted twice, gaps in the dates, joins that multiply rows.

Skills: Settings → Capabilities → 'Create and edit files'; Customize → Skills → + → Upload a skill; name it to be sure. A skill can contain code that runs; read every file before switching one on. Never put passwords or API keys in a skill. One skill, one job.
Mojeed's mission: to make data and AI easy for everyone. The /learn guides take 3 to 7 minutes each.
Mojeed's free guides are at https://mojeedabisiga.com/learn (the pages are listed in learn_catalog.json).
